svg.text: Procure-to-Pay (P2P) — High-level Workflow & SAP / ERP Data Flow
SAP PR → release → RFQ → quotation → technical & commercial evaluation → PO → GRN → invoice → payment. Numbers match the steps in P2P_Business_Process.md.
Output: Approved PR available in P2P
Output: RFQ configured with specs, vendors, T&C
Output: PO in SAP linked to RFQ
Material · Vendor · Purchasing group · Plant / Location
SAP / ERP data workflow — integration touchpoints
What moves between SAP, P2P, the Vendor Portal and invoice automation, and when.
Created / changed in SAP; periodic sync
Material MM01 (MARA) · Vendor / BP XK01, BP (LFA1)
Material code, description, UoM, vendor no., vendor category & contact, purchasing group, plant
PR saved or changed in SAP
PR no., line items, material code, qty, UoM, value, purchasing group, plant / location, requester, category
Release status; on Reject the PR returns to the requester to update and resubmit
RFQ / quotation ME41 / ME47 · EKKO (doc type AN)
ERP RFQ no. (61000…), winning vendor per line, awarded unit price, P2P RFQ reference
PO no. (4500…) returned to P2P; RFQ ref, vendor, lines, price, location, purchasing group
Material document (5000…), received qty per PO line — unlocks invoicing in the Vendor Portal
Park MIR7 → post MIRO · RBKP / RSEG
Vendor invoice no., net + VAT amount, PO ref, park no., FI document (5105…); routing by purchasing group + PO location
Payment run / manual payment by Accounts
Payment reference, paid date → invoice and PO status "Paid"

Notes: SAP T-codes and tables are typical ECC / S/4HANA objects shown for reference — confirm against the actual interface design. PO is assumed to be created in SAP from P2P because the GRN (step 21) is posted in SAP against it. Document-number ranges follow the P2P demo application.
